title: Distinguishing sodium-ion penetration and sustained transport in realistic hard carbon nanostructures
summary: Hard carbons are promising anodes for sodium-ion energy storage, yet the relationship between their heterogeneous microstructure and sodium transport remains poorly understood. Here, we combine machine-learning-generated hard-carbon structures with molecular dynamics simulations of explicit 1 M NaPF6 in ethylene carbonate/dimethyl carbonate electrolyte to investigate sodium storage and transport across carbon structures with densities from 0.5 to 2.0 g cm-3. Increasing carbon density produces less accessible pore networks and greater graphitic local ordering, allowing the influence of microstructure on electrochemical response and Na+ transport to be examined systematically. Sodium uptake increases with applied potential but decreases strongly with carbon density, while electrode charging persists even in the densest structure, where Na+ uptake remains very small. Coordination analysis shows increasing interaction with the carbon framework under applied potential, while Na+ retains a partially solvated environment. Three-dimensional trajectory analysis reveals heterogeneous, predominantly tortuous transport pathways, with the more open HC-C1 structure supporting broader penetration and greater sustained displacement. Maximum penetration depth and retained displacement are not equivalent: ions can transiently reach deep regions of denser carbon structures before returning towards the electrolyte interface. Potential-of-mean-force analysis further shows that deep penetration occurs across a range of projected free-energy changes and cannot be described by a single energetic criterion. These results show that Na+ storage and transport are governed by the interplay between electrostatic driving force, electrolyte solvation, pore accessibility and confinement, highlighting carbon microstructure as a key determinant of sustained ionic penetration.

AI.tldr: This study investigates sodium storage and transport in hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries using machine learning-generated structures and molecular dynamics simulations with explicit electrolyte. It systematically examines how carbon density (0.5-2.0 g/cm³) affects pore accessibility, graphitic ordering, Na+ uptake, coordination environment, and transport pathways.
AI.motivation: Hard carbons are promising anodes for sodium-ion energy storage, but the relationship between their heterogeneous microstructure and sodium transport remains poorly understood. This work aims to fill this knowledge gap by systematically investigating how carbon density influences sodium storage and transport mechanisms.
AI.method: The researchers combined machine-learning-generated hard carbon structures with molecular dynamics simulations of explicit 1 M NaPF6 in ethylene carbonate/dimethyl carbonate electrolyte. They examined carbon structures with densities ranging from 0.5 to 2.0 g/cm³, analyzing sodium uptake, coordination, three-dimensional trajectory, and potential-of-mean-force.
AI.result: Key findings include: (1) Sodium uptake increases with applied potential but decreases with carbon density; (2) Denser carbons have less accessible pore networks and greater graphitic local ordering; (3) Na+ retains partially solvated environment while increasingly interacting with carbon framework; (4) Transport pathways are heterogeneous and predominantly tortuous; (5) More open structures support broader penetration and greater sustained displacement; (6) Ions can transiently reach deep regions of denser carbons before returning to electrolyte interface; (7) Deep penetration occurs across a range of projected free-energy changes.
AI.conclusion: Na+ storage and transport are governed by the interplay between electrostatic driving force, electrolyte solvation, pore accessibility, and confinement. Carbon microstructure is a key determinant of sustained ionic penetration. These insights highlight the importance of engineering hard carbon microstructure for optimal sodium-ion battery performance.

title: Fractionalization-Induced Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking at Continuous Superconducting Transitions in Low-Symmetry Kondo Lattices
summary: In conventional Landau theory, simultaneous continuous onset of superconductivity and the breaking of additional symmetries generally requires a multidimensional order parameter or fine tuning. We show that symmetry fractionalization provides a different route. In a Kondo lattice with a $\mathbb Z_2$ spin liquid, the Kondo fields inherit the projective symmetry action of the spinons. When the projective time-reversal action on these fields squares to $-1$, the projective symmetry algebra forbids a condensate that preserves time-reversal symmetry and enforces twofold degeneracy of the critical modes. Because Kondo condensation in a $\mathbb Z_2$ spin liquid also breaks electromagnetic $U(1)$ symmetry, superconductivity and time-reversal symmetry breaking can emerge at a single continuous transition, even if crystal symmetry admits only one-dimensional irreducible representations. We demonstrate this mechanism in an anisotropic Kondo-Kitaev model, where superconductivity and the breaking of time-reversal and mirror symmetries emerge simultaneously.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that symmetry fractionalization in a Kondo lattice with Z2 spin liquid provides an alternative route to simultaneous continuous onset of superconductivity and time-reversal symmetry breaking without requiring multidimensional order parameters or fine tuning, demonstrated in an anisotropic Kondo-Kitaev model.
AI.motivation: In conventional Landau theory, simultaneous continuous onset of superconductivity and breaking of additional symmetries typically requires multidimensional order parameters or fine tuning. This work seeks a different mechanism that avoids these requirements.
AI.method: The authors investigate how Kondo fields inherit projective symmetry action from spinons in a Z2 spin liquid. They examine the projective time-reversal action on these fields and analyze the projective symmetry algebra constraints. The mechanism is demonstrated in an anisotropic Kondo-Kitaev model.
AI.result: When the projective time-reversal action squares to -1, the projective symmetry algebra forbids a condensate that preserves time-reversal symmetry and enforces twofold degeneracy of critical modes. Since Kondo condensation also breaks electromagnetic U(1) symmetry, superconductivity and time-reversal symmetry breaking emerge at a single continuous transition, even with only one-dimensional irreducible representations of crystal symmetry.
AI.conclusion: This mechanism allows superconductivity, time-reversal symmetry breaking, and mirror symmetry breaking to emerge simultaneously at a continuous quantum critical point in the Kondo-Kitaev model, providing a new paradigm for coupled symmetry breaking transitions in strongly correlated electron systems.

title: LATHE: LAnguage-driven Toolkit for Hypothesis-based crystal Editing
summary: Manipulating crystal structures towards targeted geometric properties or symmetry constraints is a longstanding challenge. Existing computational frameworks fall short: LLMs have poor spatial awareness and operate at coarse granularity in the token space, while diffusion- and gradient-based structure generation approaches generally produce complete structures \textit{de novo} rather allowing for fine-grained editing of a given input under arbitrary constraints. We present LATHE, a geometric toolkit that closes this gap by expressing seven classes of crystallographic properties --- bond length, bond angle, dihedral angle, coordination environment, lattice parameters, cell volume, and space group, as differentiable objectives to enable direct geometric editing of crystal structures. To demonstrate its usage in materials design, we further expose LATHE through a Model Context Protocol server and embed it in a closed-loop multi-agent system which translates hypotheses intogeometric modifications in natural language towards a given design objective. Across single-property benchmarks, LATHE attains near-perfect constraint satisfaction on all seven property types while keeping optimized structures close to local energy minima. The LATHE-equipped agent translates over 87.5\% of natural-language prompts into valid executable configurations and faithfully completes them. In a band-gap inverse-design case study, the multi-agent loop reaches the target tolerance window in nine of ten independent runs at a typical cost of thirteen hypothesis-evaluation cycles. By bridging natural-language hypothesis generation and physically grounded gradient-based structural editing, this work establishes a paradigm for interpretable, closed-loop computational materials discovery that is immediately applicable to a broad class of functional material design tasks.

AI.tldr: LATHE is a geometric toolkit that enables direct editing of crystal structures by expressing seven crystallographic properties (bond length, bond angle, dihedral angle, coordination environment, lattice parameters, cell volume, and space group) as differentiable objectives. It is integrated with a Model Context Protocol server and embedded in a closed-loop multi-agent system that translates natural language hypotheses into geometric modifications for materials design.
AI.motivation: Existing computational frameworks have significant limitations: LLMs have poor spatial awareness and operate at coarse granularity, while diffusion- and gradient-based approaches generate structures de novo rather than allowing fine-grained editing under arbitrary constraints. There was a need for a method that enables direct geometric editing of crystal structures under targeted symmetry and geometric constraints.
AI.method: LATHE expresses seven classes of crystallographic properties as differentiable objectives to enable gradient-based structural editing. The toolkit is exposed through a Model Context Protocol server and embedded in a closed-loop multi-agent system that translates natural language hypotheses into executable geometric modifications toward a given design objective.
AI.result: Across single-property benchmarks, LATHE achieves near-perfect constraint satisfaction on all seven property types while keeping optimized structures close to local energy minima. The multi-agent system translates over 87.5% of natural-language prompts into valid executable configurations. In a band-gap inverse-design case study, the system reached the target tolerance window in 9 out of 10 independent runs at a cost of approximately thirteen hypothesis-evaluation cycles.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a paradigm for interpretable, closed-loop computational materials discovery by bridging natural-language hypothesis generation and physically grounded gradient-based structural editing, which is immediately applicable to a broad class of functional material design tasks.

title: Correlated Metals, Metamagnetism, and Orbital Nematic Order in moiré Materials with Neural Quantum States
summary: In this work, we investigate a continuum model of two-dimensional electrons interacting via long-range Coulomb forces and subject to a triangular periodic potential at filling factor $ν=2$. Using neural quantum states based on message-passing neural networks optimized with variational Monte Carlo, we determine the ground-state phase diagram as a function of periodic potential strength and Zeeman field. Although the noninteracting system is expected to form a conventional band insulator, we show that strong correlations can qualitatively reshape the insulating state and, in part of the phase diagram, suppress the band insulator in favor of a correlated metallic phase, with a first-order transition separating the two regimes. Moreover, the metal--insulator transition exhibits a strong dependence on spin polarization: the unpolarized system becomes insulating at substantially weaker periodic potentials through the formation of an $s$-wave molecular insulator, where opposite-spin electrons bind near each potential minimum, whereas the fully polarized system requires a significantly deeper potential and instead forms a symmetry-broken orbital nematic molecular crystal. This spin-dependent molecular transition gives rise to discontinuous magnetization curves, metamagnetic transitions, and several multicritical points in the phase diagram, together with clear signatures in the density profiles, real-space correlation functions, and structure factors. To further elucidate the role of the long-range character of the Coulomb interaction, we also study short-range repulsive interactions, which can be realized with ultracold-atom platforms. We find that the qualitative structure of the many-body phase diagram remains unchanged, demonstrating the robustness of our results across different interaction models.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a continuum model of 2D electrons with long-range Coulomb interactions under a triangular periodic potential at filling factor ν=2, using neural quantum states (message-passing neural networks) with variational Monte Carlo to map out the ground-state phase diagram as a function of periodic potential strength and Zeeman field.
AI.motivation: The noninteracting system is expected to form a conventional band insulator, but the authors hypothesize that strong correlations can qualitatively reshape this insulating state, leading to novel phases that depend on spin polarization.
AI.method: Neural quantum states based on message-passing neural networks optimized with variational Monte Carlo were used to study the system. The authors also compared long-range Coulomb interactions with short-range repulsive interactions (relevant for ultracold atom platforms).
AI.result: Strong correlations can suppress the band insulator in favor of a correlated metallic phase with a first-order transition. The metal-insulator transition depends heavily on spin polarization: unpolarized systems become insulating at weaker potentials via an s-wave molecular insulator, while fully polarized systems require deeper potentials and form an orbital nematic molecular crystal. The phase diagram exhibits discontinuous magnetization curves, metamagnetic transitions, and multicritical points.
AI.conclusion: The qualitative structure of the many-body phase diagram remains unchanged when replacing long-range Coulomb interactions with short-range repulsive interactions, demonstrating the robustness of these results across different interaction models and their relevance to both electronic systems and ultracold atom platforms.

title: Finite-momentum pairing and magnetic halos in a spin-imbalanced Holstein model
summary: Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconductivity, Cooper pairing at finite-momentum driven by spin imbalance, remains difficult to study numerically in two dimensions. The fermion sign problem in the spin-imbalanced attractive Hubbard model severely limits quantum Monte Carlo access to the low temperatures where pairing correlations are most pronounced. We show that the Holstein model, in which the effective attraction is retarded by phonon dynamics, strongly suppresses sign fluctuations under spin imbalance, enabling unbiased determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations deep in this regime. With increasing magnetization, zero-momentum pairing evolves into finite-momentum FFLO pairing, evidenced by oscillating real-space pair correlations and a shift of the pairing susceptibility peak to finite $\vec{Q}$. The finite-momentum susceptibility substantially exceeds its zero-momentum value. At high density $n \sim 0.875$, near magnetization $m \approx 1-n$ where the majority-spin density approaches half filling, FFLO pairing coexists with checkerboard charge-density-wave order at short range, while staggered longitudinal spin correlations emerge as a magnetic halo at larger distances. These spatial textures provide experimentally accessible signatures of finite-momentum pairing and motivate cold-atom realizations of FFLO physics.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconductivity in a 2D Holstein model with spin imbalance using determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations. The study demonstrates that phonon dynamics suppress the fermion sign problem, enabling exploration of finite-momentum pairing at low temperatures.
AI.motivation: FFLO superconductivity (Cooper pairing at finite momentum driven by spin imbalance) is difficult to study numerically in 2D due to the severe fermion sign problem in spin-imbalanced attractive Hubbard models, which limits quantum Monte Carlo access to low temperatures where pairing correlations are strongest.
AI.method: The researchers used determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations on the Holstein model, where effective attraction is retarded by phonon dynamics. This model choice was strategic because it strongly suppresses sign fluctuations under spin imbalance, enabling unbiased simulations deep in the FFLO regime.
AI.result: With increasing magnetization, zero-momentum pairing evolves into finite-momentum FFLO pairing, evidenced by: (1) oscillating real-space pair correlations, (2) a shift of the pairing susceptibility peak to finite momentum Q, and (3) finite-momentum susceptibility substantially exceeding zero-momentum value. At high density (n ~ 0.875) near magnetization m ≈ 1-n, FFLO pairing coexists with checkerboard charge-density-wave order at short range, while staggered longitudinal spin correlations emerge as a magnetic halo at larger distances.
AI.conclusion: The spatial textures observed provide experimentally accessible signatures of finite-momentum pairing and motivate cold-atom realizations of FFLO physics.

title: Temperature--Composition Mapping and Growth-History Dependence of rBN-Related Raman Responses in BN Grown on Fe--B under Flowing N$_2$
summary: BN products formed on Fe--B sources under flowing N$_2$ were investigated primarily at 1250--1400~$^\circ$C over nominal B contents of 1--10~wt\% to determine how rBN-related Raman character depends on growth condition and history. Spatially resolved Raman mapping across 44 growth conditions identified a restricted temperature--composition region in which the integrated rBN-related low-frequency response over 750--835~cm$^{-1}$, $A_{750-835}$, is strongly developed together with the integrated total response of the main $\sim$1367~cm$^{-1}$ BN band, $A_{1367}^{\rm{total}}$. In addition, the asymmetric high-wavenumber extension of the $\sim$1367~cm$^{-1}$ band was quantified by subtracting a symmetric fitted core and integrating the far high-wavenumber residual, $T_{\rm{high}}^{\rm{far}}$. The independently defined $A_{750-835}$ and $T_{\rm{high}}^{\rm{far}}$ responses exhibit a strong correspondence across the full dataset, supporting their use as complementary rBN-related Raman observables. In contrast, $A_{750-835}/A_{1367}^{\rm{total}}$ varies systematically among growth conditions, indicating that the relative prominence of the low-frequency response changes with temperature and composition rather than tracking the overall BN response through a fixed proportionality. Growth-duration experiments at 1350~$^\circ$C further show that this ratio also depends on high-temperature N$_2$ dwell time, establishing growth history as an additional kinetic variable. Powder X-ray diffraction on selected products independently confirms the presence of rBN-related stacking, while second-harmonic generation provides complementary symmetry-sensitive evidence. These results define a processing window favorable for strong rBN-related Raman response and introduce a quantitative framework for tracking both the low-frequency and band-asymmetry signatures associated with rBN-related BN structure.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates boron nitride (BN) products formed on Fe-B sources at 1250-1400°C with varying B content (1-10 wt%). The study identifies Raman spectroscopy markers for rhombohedral BN (rBN) formation, specifically focusing on low-frequency responses (750-835 cm⁻¹) and high-wavenumber band asymmetry of the main ~1367 cm⁻¹ BN band. The research establishes a processing window favorable for rBN formation and introduces quantitative metrics for tracking rBN-related structural features.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to understand how rBN-related Raman characteristics depend on growth conditions (temperature, composition) and history (dwell time) in BN products synthesized from Fe-B sources under flowing N₂. The authors aim to identify reliable spectroscopic markers for rBN formation and establish a quantitative framework for tracking rBN-related structural features.
AI.method: The study employed: (1) Spatially resolved Raman mapping across 44 growth conditions, (2) Quantitative analysis of low-frequency response (A750-835), main BN band (A1367 total), and high-wavenumber band asymmetry (Thigh far), (3) Growth-duration experiments at 1350°C to investigate kinetic effects, (4) Powder X-ray diffraction for independent confirmation of rBN-related stacking, and (5) Second-harmonic generation for symmetry-sensitive evidence.
AI.result: The study identified a restricted temperature-composition region where both A750-835 and A1367 total are strongly developed. A strong correspondence exists between independently defined A750-835 and Thigh far responses across the full dataset. However, the ratio A750-835/A1367 total varies systematically with temperature and composition, indicating the relative prominence of low-frequency response depends on growth conditions rather than tracking overall BN response proportionally. Growth-duration experiments at 1350°C showed this ratio also depends on high-temperature N₂ dwell time, establishing growth history as an additional kinetic variable.
AI.conclusion: The research defines a processing window favorable for strong rBN-related Raman response and introduces a quantitative framework for tracking both low-frequency and band-asymmetry signatures associated with rBN-related BN structure. The correspondence between A750-835 and Thigh far provides complementary rBN-related Raman observables, while the variable ratio A750-835/A1367 total indicates that relative rBN content depends on temperature, composition, and growth duration.

title: Melting phase diagram of the two-dimensional electron solid in a perpendicular magnetic field
summary: We determine the thermal melting phase diagram of the electron solid by measuring the onset density of the double-threshold voltage-current curves in the insulating state in the ultra-high mobility two-dimensional electron system in SiGe/Si/SiGe quantum wells at different temperatures in perpendicular magnetic fields. The introduction of a magnetic field leads to a considerable increase in the onset density, which is strongest at the lowest temperatures and decreases with increasing temperature, and the melting temperature increases with magnetic field. These data are in agreement with theoretical predictions. Unexpectedly, the melting temperature as a function of electron density in a fixed magnetic field reveals a plateau, which can be interpreted in terms of resonance modes in the crystallites.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the thermal melting phase diagram of electron solids in ultra-high mobility SiGe/Si/SiGe quantum wells by measuring double-threshold voltage-current curves at different temperatures and magnetic fields. The research reveals that magnetic fields significantly increase the onset density, with the strongest effect at low temperatures, and demonstrates an unexpected plateau in melting temperature versus electron density.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to determine and understand the thermal melting phase diagram of the electron solid in a two-dimensional electron system, particularly to verify theoretical predictions about how magnetic fields affect the phase transition between insulating electron solid and conducting states.
AI.method: The researchers measured the onset density of double-threshold voltage-current curves in the insulating state using ultra-high mobility two-dimensional electron systems in SiGe/Si/SiGe quantum wells. Measurements were conducted at different temperatures and perpendicular magnetic fields.
AI.result: The magnetic field leads to a considerable increase in onset density, which is strongest at the lowest temperatures and decreases with increasing temperature. The melting temperature increases with magnetic field. Unexpectedly, a plateau was observed in the melting temperature as a function of electron density at fixed magnetic field, which can be interpreted in terms of resonance modes in crystallites.
AI.conclusion: The experimental data agree with theoretical predictions. The unexpected plateau phenomenon suggests the presence of resonance modes in the crystallites, providing new insights into the nature of electron solid melting transitions in 2D systems under magnetic fields.

title: Emergent Noncoplanar Spin Chirality through Magnetic and Nonmagnetic Substitution in the Kagome Antiferromagnet Mn$_3$Sn
comment: Accepted for publication in Materials Today Physics, 35 pages, 8 figures
summary: Controlling noncoplanar spin textures in centrosymmetric magnets remains a central challenge for realizing emergent Berry-phase phenomena. Here, we demonstrate that magnetic (Cr) and nonmagnetic (Cu) substitution at the Mn site provide distinct routes to engineer spin chirality and topological transport in the kagome antiferromagnet Mn$_3$Sn. Cr substitution enhances low-temperature spin canting, stabilizing a dense noncoplanar texture that yields a pronounced topological Hall effect (THE) at low temperatures. In contrast, Cu substitution drives a spin-reorientation transition accompanied by an easy-axis rotation, creating a broad temperature window (150--208 K) where competing magnetic anisotropies stabilize noncoplanar spin textures and generate a large THE. A concurrent carrier-type crossover signals an underlying electronic-structure reconstruction. These results reveal that exchange enhancement and exchange dilution represent two fundamentally different pathways for tuning real-space Berry curvature, establishing chemical substitution as a powerful strategy for engineering topological transport in kagome antiferromagnets.

AI.tldr: This study demonstrates that Cr and Cu substitution at the Mn site in kagome antiferromagnet Mn3Sn provide distinct pathways for engineering spin chirality and topological transport. Cr enhances low-temperature spin canting, while Cu drives a spin-reorientation transition with easy-axis rotation, creating a broad temperature window (150-208 K) with large topological Hall effect.
AI.motivation: Controlling noncoplanar spin textures in centrosymmetric magnets remains a central challenge for realizing emergent Berry-phase phenomena.
AI.method: Magnetic (Cr) and nonmagnetic (Cu) substitution at the Mn site in kagome antiferromagnet Mn3Sn, with transport and magnetic measurements to characterize spin textures and topological Hall effect.
AI.result: Cr substitution enhances low-temperature spin canting, stabilizing a dense noncoplanar texture with pronounced THE at low temperatures. Cu substitution drives a spin-reorientation transition with easy-axis rotation, creating a broad temperature window (150-208 K) where competing magnetic anisotropies stabilize noncoplanar spin textures and generate a large THE, accompanied by a carrier-type crossover.
AI.conclusion: Exchange enhancement (Cr) and exchange dilution (Cu) represent two fundamentally different pathways for tuning real-space Berry curvature, establishing chemical substitution as a powerful strategy for engineering topological transport in kagome antiferromagnets.

title: Consistent perturbation expansions in screened interactions
summary: Many-body perturbation theory is a powerful framework to calculate spectroscopic quantities, as well as the total energy. However, the field suffers from the fact that different flavors of approximations lead to a wide range of results. We present several in principle exact expansions and discuss how to use them consistently. We concentrate on the first two orders in the respective screened Coulomb interaction. Of special interest is a consistent expansion around the Kohn-Sham system. We illustrate the performance of the various choices using the symmetric Hubbard dimer over a wide range of correlation strength. In particular, the expansion based on exact Kohn-Sham ingredients stands out as a promising route towards good energies and good spectra.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the problem of inconsistencies and wide range of results when using different approximations in many-body perturbation theory for calculating spectroscopic quantities and total energy. The authors propose several in principle exact expansions, focusing on the first two orders in the screened Coulomb interaction, with special emphasis on a consistent expansion around the Kohn-Sham system. The symmetric Hubbard dimer is used to test various approaches across different correlation strengths, demonstrating that the expansion based on exact Kohn-Sham ingredients provides promising results for both energies and spectra.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the issue of inconsistency and variability in results when different approximation flavors are used in many-body perturbation theory calculations. The field lacks a systematic way to obtain reliable spectroscopic quantities and total energies.
AI.method: The authors present several in principle exact expansions and discuss their consistent use, focusing on the first two orders in the screened Coulomb interaction. They particularly emphasize developing a consistent expansion around the Kohn-Sham system. The methodology is illustrated using the symmetric Hubbard dimer as a test case across a wide range of correlation strengths.
AI.result: The expansion based on exact Kohn-Sham ingredients stands out as a promising route, providing good energies and good spectra. This suggests that this approach offers a more reliable and consistent method compared to other approximation flavors.
AI.conclusion: A consistent expansion around the Kohn-Sham system, particularly using exact Kohn-Sham ingredients, offers a promising direction for achieving accurate results in both energy and spectroscopic calculations within many-body perturbation theory.

title: Orientation refinement for nanobeam precession electron diffraction patterns using spot intensity profiles
summary: We develop a method to measure crystallographic orientations with high angular resolution for nano-beam precession electron diffraction patterns, and applicable to 4D scanning precession electron diffraction. We show that internal variations of intensity in the diffraction spots can be simulated and correlated to experimental variations to measure the crystallographic orientation with a much better angular resolution that with the standard method of automated crystal orientation mapping (ACOM). In a tilt series carried out with long exposure time on a monocrystal of silicon around the main goniometer tilt axis, the imposed tilt angles are retrieved with a 0.044° to 0.054° precision with refinement, against 0.25° to 0.33° with the standard method. Shorter exposure times, introducing Poisson noise, marginally degrade the precision to a 0.054° to 0.066° range. The method also corrects a systematic error of ACOM near zone axis.

AI.tldr: A method to measure crystallographic orientations with high angular resolution (0.044°-0.066°) for nano-beam precession electron diffraction patterns, significantly improving upon standard ACOM precision (0.25°-0.33%) by using intensity variations in diffraction spots.
AI.motivation: Standard automated crystal orientation mapping (ACOM) has limited angular resolution (~0.25°-0.33°) for measuring crystallographic orientations in precession electron diffraction, and exhibits systematic errors near zone axis. Higher precision is needed for detailed crystallographic analysis.
AI.method: The method simulates internal intensity variations in diffraction spots and correlates these simulations to experimental variations. Applied to 4D scanning precession electron diffraction data. Tested via tilt series on monocrystalline silicon with long exposure times, then validated with shorter exposures introducing Poisson noise.
AI.result: With refinement and long exposure, precision improved to 0.044°-0.054° vs 0.25°-0.33° for standard ACOM. With shorter exposures (Poisson noise), precision degraded marginally to 0.054°-0.066°. The method also corrects systematic errors of ACOM near zone axis.
AI.conclusion: This intensity-based refinement method provides ~5-7x better angular resolution than standard ACOM, with robust performance even with noisy data, offering significant improvement for crystallographic orientation mapping in electron microscopy applications.

title: Decohering Kitaev's Sixteenfold Way: A Holographic Approach
summary: We study anyon decoherence in 2D topological order, with the fermion decoherence in Kitaev's sixteenfold way as explicit examples. The sixteenfold way includes chiral topological phases, which are believed to admit no commuting projector Hamiltonian, making it challenging to study their decoherence directly. We further conjecture the density matrix produced by this decoherence induced phase transition can be obtained by a three-step procedure: first lift the topological order to its Walker-Wang model, followed by a transition to another Walker-Wang model, and finally trace over the bulk degrees of freedom. This establishes a connection between the decoherence of a topological order and a pure state phase transition in its 3D counterpart. Many examples are given. In particular, we show that decohering the fermion in each of the sixteen states always yields an intrinsically mixed-state topological order, a consequence of the fact the corresponding 3D bulk always transits into the 3D fermionic toric code (fTC). Our result suggests a systematic method for studying anyon decoherence in chiral topological orders at the level of commuting projector Hamiltonians.

AI.tldr: This paper studies anyon decoherence in 2D topological order using Kitaev's sixteenfold way as examples. The authors propose a three-step procedure connecting 2D decoherence to 3D phase transitions, and demonstrate that fermion decoherence in all sixteen states produces intrinsically mixed-state topological orders linked to the 3D fermionic toric code.
AI.motivation: The study addresses anyon decoherence in 2D topological order, particularly in chiral topological phases of Kitaev's sixteenfold way that are believed to lack commuting projector Hamiltonians, making direct study challenging.
AI.method: The paper employs a three-step procedure: (1) lifting topological order to Walker-Wang model, (2) transitioning to another Walker-Wang model, and (3) tracing over bulk degrees of freedom. This connects decoherence of 2D topological order to pure state phase transitions in 3D counterparts.
AI.result: Decohering the fermion in each of the sixteen states always yields an intrinsically mixed-state topological order, because the corresponding 3D bulk transitions into the 3D fermionic toric code (fTC).
AI.conclusion: The result establishes a systematic method for studying anyon decoherence in chiral topological orders via commuting projector Hamiltonians, specifically showing that decohering the fermion in the sixteenfold way always yields intrinsically mixed-state topological orders transitioning to 3D fermionic toric code.

title: Optimizing the magnetic hyperthermia efficiency from the structural dependence of dipolar interactions in magnetic nanoparticles assemblies
summary: Magnetic hyperthermia, based on the conversion of the magnetic energy of magnetic nanoparticles (MNP) under an alternating external field into heat, presents a great interest, especially because of important applications such as promising advances in cancer treatment. The underlying frequency-dependent response of the MNP assembly under the excitation field depends on the first hand on the individual properties of the MNP such as their size, shape and magnetocrystalline anisotropy and on the other hand on collective properties generated by interactions between MNP. Due to the long-range dipolar component of the latter, the first consequence is the so-called demagnetizing effects, making the response dependent on the external sample shape. This is the reason for studying the properties of MNP in assemblies of anisotropic external shapes such as films, chains, or elongated aggregates. In the present work, using a recently developed Time Quantified Monte Carlo (TQMC) framework for dynamic simulations, we focus more precisely on the importance of the local structure in such anisotropic aggregates to the dipolar interactions contribution of the response to the external field. Here the local structure is understood as both the location of the nanoparticles and the distribution of their easy axes. We show that the latter must be determined in a self-consistent way starting with the equilibrium structure of a ferrofluid modeled as the dipolar hard sphere fluid.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates magnetic hyperthermia using magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs), focusing on how local structure (nanoparticle positions and easy axis distribution) in anisotropic aggregates affects the dipolar interactions and response to external alternating fields. The study uses Time Quantified Monte Carlo (TQMC) simulations and emphasizes that easy axis distribution must be determined self-consistently from the equilibrium structure of a ferrofluid modeled as dipolar hard sphere fluid.
AI.motivation: Magnetic hyperthermia shows great promise for cancer treatment, but the response of MNP assemblies under alternating fields depends on both individual particle properties and collective inter-particle interactions. The long-range dipolar interactions cause demagnetizing effects that depend on sample shape, necessitating study of anisotropic aggregates like films, chains, and elongated structures. However, the importance of local structure (particle locations and easy axis distribution) in such anisotropic aggregates remains unclear.
AI.method: The researchers employed a Time Quantified Monte Carlo (TQMC) framework for dynamic simulations to study MNP assemblies. They focused on anisotropic external shapes (films, chains, elongated aggregates) and investigated how local structure—specifically nanoparticle positions and easy axis distribution—contributes to dipolar interactions and field response. The easy axis distribution was determined in a self-consistent manner starting from the equilibrium structure of a ferrofluid modeled as the dipolar hard sphere fluid.
AI.result: The study demonstrates the critical importance of local structure in anisotropic MNP aggregates. The easy axis distribution of nanoparticles must be determined self-consistently from the equilibrium ferrofluid structure (dipolar hard sphere fluid), rather than assumed arbitrarily. This approach reveals how local structure significantly influences the dipolar interactions contribution to the overall response under external alternating fields.
AI.conclusion: Local structure (nanoparticle positions and easy axis distribution) plays a crucial role in determining the magnetic response of MNP assemblies in anisotropic aggregates. The self-consistent determination of easy axis distribution from equilibrium ferrofluid structure provides a more accurate representation of dipolar interactions, which is essential for optimizing magnetic hyperthermia applications in cancer treatment.

title: Ab initio design of enhanced and sign-reversible spin Hall and spin Nernst conductivity in skutterudite materials
summary: The search for novel materials capable of robust spin-current generation remains an active area of research. Here, we investigate the intrinsic spin Hall and spin Nernst effects in Co- and Rh-based skutterudites and explore their enhancement through heavy-metal substitution and site-selective doping. Using first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding models, we analyze the spin Berry curvature and spin-transport responses of pristine MX$_3$, where M = Co, Rh and X = As, Sb, as well as chemically modified systems. Despite sizable momentum-resolved spin Berry curvature, the pristine compounds exhibit relatively small net spin Hall responses due to substantial cancellation across the Brillouin zone. Isoelectronic Ir and Bi substitution at 8$c$ Wycoff M site produces little enhancement near the E$_F$, whereas non-isoelectronic Pt substitution yields a relatively better response. Most interestingly, the incorporation of Pt at the interstitial $2a$ Wycoff site of RhAs$_3$ nearly doubles the spin Hall conductivity to $\sim400~(\hbar/e)(Ω,\mathrm{cm})^{-1}$ near the E$_F$ when compared to Pt substitution at 8$c$ position. At 300 K, the same interstitially filled system exhibits a spin Nernst conductivity of $\sim1.46~(\hbar/e),\mathrm{A,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$ at the E$_F$, nearly an order of magnitude larger than that of $M$-site Pt substitution. The enhanced responses arise from Pt $5d$ states, strong spin-orbit coupling, and avoided crossings that generate pronounced spin-Berry-curvature hot spots. These results demonstrate that site-selective chemical engineering can effectively overcome momentum-space cancellation resulting in enhanced spin Hall and spin Nernst responses in skutterudites. Our results provide a possible route towards robust spin-current generation in this class of materials.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates intrinsic spin Hall and spin Nernst effects in Co- and Rh-based skutterudites using first-principles calculations, demonstrating that site-selective Pt doping at interstitial sites can nearly double spin Hall conductivity to ~400 (ℏ/e)(Ω·cm)⁻¹ and achieve spin Nernst conductivity of ~1.46 (ℏ/e) A·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ at 300 K.
AI.motivation: The search for novel materials capable of robust spin-current generation is an active research area. The authors aim to enhance spin Hall and spin Nernst responses in skutterudite compounds through heavy-metal substitution and site-selective doping.
AI.method: First-principles calculations combined with Wannier-based tight-binding models were used to analyze spin Berry curvature and spin-transport responses of pristine MX₃ (M = Co, Rh; X = As, Sb) and chemically modified systems.
AI.result: Pristine compounds show small net spin Hall responses due to momentum-space cancellation despite sizable spin Berry curvature. Ir and Bi substitution at M sites shows little enhancement, while Pt substitution is better. Most importantly, Pt at interstitial 2a site of RhAs₃ nearly doubles spin Hall conductivity to ~400 (ℏ/e)(Ω·cm)⁻¹ compared to M-site Pt substitution. At 300 K, the interstitial system shows spin Nernst conductivity of ~1.46 (ℏ/e) A·m⁻¹·K⁻¹, nearly an order of magnitude larger than M-site Pt substitution.
AI.conclusion: Site-selective chemical engineering can effectively overcome momentum-space cancellation and enhance spin Hall and spin Nernst responses in skutterudites, providing a viable route toward robust spin-current generation in this material class.

title: Coercivity-Aware Machine Learning Discovery of Rare-Earth-Free Soft Magnetic Alloys with First-Principles Magnetic Benchmarks
summary: Coercivity-aware machine learning is developed to screen rare-earth-free soft magnetic alloys using Curie temperature and coercivity as coupled design targets. A compiled experimental magnetic-material dataset is evaluated using composition-grouped partitioning to avoid overlap of identical compositions between training and testing, and elemental fractions and composition-weighted elemental descriptors are examined for prediction of the two magnetic properties. Residual-based prediction intervals and distance-to-training filters are then incorporated to screen Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Al-Si compositions. Composition-grouped evaluation shows lower predictive accuracy than conventional random partitioning, demonstrating the importance of evaluating transfer to previously unseen compositions. Combining weighted elemental descriptors with elemental fractions improves Curie-temperature prediction, whereas the additional descriptors do not improve coercivity prediction, consistent with the strong dependence of coercivity on processing and microstructure. Uncertainty-aware screening substantially narrows the candidate space and identifies Fe-Co-rich compositions for further evaluation. First-principles calculations independently show strong magnetic polarization and magnetovolume effects in representative Fe-Co structures, while finite-temperature atomistic spin simulations place the Fe-Co benchmark systems on high magnetic-ordering-temperature scales. The combined approach provides a computational framework for prioritizing rare-earth-free soft-magnetic chemistries while distinguishing composition-level screening from candidate-specific physical validation.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a coercivity-aware machine learning framework to screen rare-earth-free soft magnetic alloys, using Curie temperature and coercivity as coupled design targets. The approach combines composition-grouped data partitioning, elemental descriptors, and uncertainty-aware screening to identify promising Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Al-Si compositions, validated by first-principles calculations and atomistic spin simulations.
AI.motivation: Rare-earth-free soft magnetic alloys are needed as sustainable alternatives to rare-earth-based magnets. The challenge is to efficiently screen large composition spaces for materials with optimal magnetic properties (Curie temperature and coercivity) while accounting for the strong dependence of coercivity on processing and microstructure.
AI.method: The study used: (1) A compiled experimental magnetic-material dataset with composition-grouped partitioning to prevent data leakage; (2) Combination of elemental fractions and composition-weighted elemental descriptors for property prediction; (3) Residual-based prediction intervals and distance-to-training filters for uncertainty-aware screening; (4) First-principles calculations for magnetic polarization and magnetovolume effects; (5) Finite-temperature atomistic spin simulations for magnetic-ordering temperature validation.
AI.result: Composition-grouped evaluation showed lower predictive accuracy than random partitioning, highlighting the importance of testing transfer to unseen compositions. Weighted elemental descriptors combined with elemental fractions improved Curie temperature prediction but not coercivity prediction, consistent with coercivity's sensitivity to processing. Uncertainty-aware screening significantly narrowed candidate compositions, identifying Fe-Co-rich compositions for further investigation.
AI.conclusion: The integrated machine learning and physics-based framework successfully provides a computational approach for prioritizing rare-earth-free soft magnetic chemistries. It effectively distinguishes between composition-level screening and candidate-specific physical validation, offering a pathway to accelerate discovery of sustainable magnetic materials.

title: Algebra of symmetry allowed physical properties of crystals
summary: The symmetry of a physical system given by the 122 magnetic point groups (MPGs) leads to only 21 sets of restrictions on any physical tensors. Those, so called, tenor forms were labeled by letters from A to U by R. R. Birss (Symmetry and Magnetism, North Holland, Amsterdam, 1964). A new concept of property-related point groups (PRPGs) is proposed. It is shown that the 21 PRPGs isomorphic to the 21 non-centrosymmetric crystallographic point groups (CPGs) corresponds to the 21 tensor forms. Therefore instead of a symbols from A to U one can use PRPGs as mathematical objects corresponding to the tenor forms. From the Neumann's principle given multipole component is only allowed in a system when a group describing symmetry of the system is a subgroup of the multipole component symmetry. Each tensor can be expressed in the terms of the multipole degrees of freedom, i.e. it corresponds to a subset of all multipole components allowed by given PRPG. Those relations leads to the algebra of tensor forms, where space of allowed tensor components and space of PRPG operators are somehow dual to each other.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the concept of Property-Related Point Groups (PRPGs) as an alternative to the traditional letter-labeled tensor forms (A-U) derived from the 122 magnetic point groups. The authors show that the 21 PRPGs are isomorphic to the 21 non-centrosymmetric crystallographic point groups, providing a more mathematically rigorous framework for describing tensor restrictions in magnetic symmetry systems.
AI.motivation: The traditional approach using Birss's letter system (A-U) for labeling tensor forms lacks mathematical elegance and direct connection to group theory. The authors aim to establish a more fundamental mathematical framework by replacing these symbolic labels with actual mathematical objects (PRPGs) that have clear group-theoretic meaning.
AI.method: The authors established isomorphism between the 21 PRPGs and the 21 non-centrosymmetric CPGs. They applied Neumann's principle to determine allowed multipole components, where a multipole component is permitted only when the system's symmetry group is a subgroup of the multipole component's symmetry. Tensor components are expressed in terms of multipole degrees of freedom, creating a dual relationship between tensor component spaces and PRPG operator spaces.
AI.result: The 21 PRPGs successfully replace the A-U tensor form labels, providing a mathematically rigorous isomorphic mapping. The framework establishes that each tensor corresponds to a specific subset of multipole components allowed by a given PRPG, revealing a dual algebraic structure between allowed tensor components and PRPG operators.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a more elegant mathematical framework for understanding tensor restrictions in magnetic systems. The PRPG approach offers better mathematical clarity and establishes a formal algebraic structure for tensor forms, though practical implementation may still require the traditional letter notation for compatibility with existing literature.

title: Second-order Raman and anharmonic lattice dynamics in lead-halide perovskites
summary: We explore the microscopic origin of THz-driven lattice dynamics in methylammonium lead bromide CH$_3$NH$_3$PbBr$_3$ using two-dimensional THz Kerr-effect spectroscopy. The analysis of the experiment enables discrimination between competing nonlinear excitation mechanisms and reveals that the dominant pathway is phonon-mediated rather than purely photonic. In particular, we argue that the commonly observed 1.15~THz Raman-active $A_g$ mode is not excited directly by the THz electric field. Instead, it emerges through cubic anharmonic coupling to an infrared-active phonon at 0.68~THz. Furthermore, a satellite feature at 1.36~THz is identified as a two-phonon Raman response of the same infrared-active mode. The observation of strong quadratic coupling involving the infrared-active phonon suggests an unconventional form of electron-phonon dressing present in lead-halide perovskites.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the microscopic origin of THz-driven lattice dynamics in CH3NH3PbBr3 using 2D THz Kerr-effect spectroscopy, revealing that the observed 1.15 THz Raman-active mode is excited through anharmonic coupling to an infrared-active phonon at 0.68 THz rather than direct THz excitation.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to understand the fundamental mechanism of THz-driven lattice dynamics in lead-halide perovskites, specifically to discriminate between competing nonlinear excitation mechanisms - whether the lattice response is driven photonically or phonon-mediated.
AI.method: The study employs two-dimensional THz Kerr-effect spectroscopy to analyze the microscopic origin of THz-driven lattice dynamics in methylammonium lead bromide (CH3NH3PbBr3).
AI.result: The dominant excitation pathway is phonon-mediated rather than purely photonic. The 1.15 THz Raman-active Ag mode is not excited directly by the THz electric field but emerges through cubic anharmonic coupling to an infrared-active phonon at 0.68 THz. A satellite feature at 1.36 THz is identified as a two-phonon Raman response of the same infrared-active mode. Strong quadratic coupling involving the infrared-active phonon suggests an unconventional form of electron-phonon dressing in lead-halide perovskites.
AI.conclusion: The commonly observed 1.15 THz Raman-active Ag mode in CH3NH3PbBr3 is excited indirectly through anharmonic coupling to an infrared-active phonon at 0.68 THz, rather than through direct THz electric field excitation. This finding reveals phonon-mediated dynamics and suggests an unconventional electron-phonon dressing mechanism in lead-halide perovskites.

title: Illuminating early ZrC oxidation using ensemble small-cell DFT with dynamic gas management
summary: During zirconium carbide oxidation, liberated carbon can remain beneath the oxide or escape as gas, complicating the interpretation of mass measurements. We adapt the small-cell ensemble method using sixteen 140 ps ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories at 873-1273 K under a sustained high oxygen flux with gas removal. The average rates of net mass gain and total carbon transfer into gas or retained chains follow Arrhenius trends. Above 973 K, gas evolution levels off while total carbon transfer increases. The fraction of transferred carbon retained in chains rises from 40 % at 973 K to 66 % at 1273 K. Fits after 40 ps suggest declining carbon transfer rates over time, although not in every trajectory. These results show that carbon partitioning during early oxidation depends on temperature, with increasing temperature above 973 K favouring chain formation over gasification.

AI.tldr: This study investigates zirconium carbide oxidation using ab initio molecular dynamics, revealing temperature-dependent carbon partitioning between gas formation and carbon chain retention, with higher temperatures favoring chain formation over gasification.
AI.motivation: The challenge in interpreting mass measurements during zirconium carbide oxidation stems from carbon's dual fate: remaining beneath the oxide or escaping as gas. This complexity motivated the development of a more sophisticated analytical approach.
AI.method: Small-cell ensemble method with sixteen 140 ps ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories at 873-1273 K under sustained high oxygen flux with gas removal.
AI.result: Net mass gain and carbon transfer follow Arrhenius trends. Above 973 K, gas evolution plateaus while total carbon transfer increases. Carbon retention in chains rises from 40% at 973 K to 66% at 1273 K. Carbon transfer rates decline after 40 ps in most trajectories.
AI.conclusion: Carbon partitioning during early oxidation is temperature-dependent. Temperatures above 973 K increasingly favor carbon chain formation over gasification, providing new insight into the oxidation mechanism.

title: Floquet density response in laser-assisted fast-electron scattering from solids
summary: We extend the Bethe--Floquet formalism of Joachain and coworkers, originally developed for laser-assisted electron--atom collisions, to inelastic scattering of fast electrons from a many-body condensed-matter target in a time-periodic light field. At first order in the projectile--target interaction, the general Floquet--Fourier cross section separates into exact laser-dressed projectile kernels and a matrix-valued Floquet density response of the target. For spatially structured or translationally non-invariant systems, the latter is the bi-momentum Floquet structure factor; its momentum diagonal defines the Floquet generalization of the dynamic structure factor, constrained by Hermiticity, positivity, and sum rules. As a controlled realization of the general projectile kernel, an eikonal--Volkov approximation for slowly varying inhomogeneous fields yields a finite-momentum-resolution convolution of the target response. In the homogeneous-field dipole limit, the projectile kernel reduces to Bessel-function sidebands and the cross section takes the familiar Bethe--Floquet form. The Floquet density correlator separates exactly into the outer product of the pump-induced coherent mean density and connected fluctuations. In the straight-trajectory nonrecoil limit, the coherent, target-elastic sector defines the weak-coupling PINEM amplitude; repeated coherent insertions generate the PINEM Bessel ladder, with an explicit no-double-counting prescription for combining this channel with connected losses. As worked examples, we evaluate the connected, target-changing cross section analytically for a metal in the Drude and diffusive limits, recovering Bessel-weighted plasmon-loss and diffusive combs, and for a driven two-level model that exhibits off-diagonal Floquet coherences through Bessel-channel interference.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the Bethe-Floquet formalism to describe laser-assisted inelastic electron scattering from many-body condensed matter targets. The theory generalizes the dynamic structure factor to the Floquet domain, provides a unified framework connecting projectile kernels to target responses, and recovers known phenomena (PINEM, plasmon losses) in appropriate limits while revealing new features like off-diagonal Floquet coherences.
AI.motivation: Extend the Bethe-Floquet formalism (originally developed for laser-assisted electron-atom collisions) to handle inelastic scattering of fast electrons from many-body condensed-matter targets in time-periodic light fields. The existing theory was limited to atomic systems and needed generalization for condensed matter applications.
AI.method: First-order expansion in the projectile-target interaction, separating the Floquet-Fourier cross section into laser-dressed projectile kernels and target's matrix-valued Floquet density response. For structured systems, uses bi-momentum Floquet structure factor. Employs eikonal-Volkov approximation for slowly varying inhomogeneous fields, yielding finite-momentum-resolution convolution. In the straight-trajectory nonrecoil limit, derives weak-coupling PINEM amplitude and Bessel ladder. Worked examples include Drude and diffusive limits of metals, and driven two-level model.
AI.result: The Floquet density response generalizes the dynamic structure factor with constraints from Hermiticity, positivity, and sum rules. The eikonal-Volkov approximation yields finite-momentum-resolution convolution of the target response. In the dipole limit, the cross section reduces to the familiar Bethe-Floquet form with Bessel-function sidebands. The theory recovers Bessel-weighted plasmon-loss and diffusive combs for metals in Drude/diffusive limits, and reveals off-diagonal Floquet coherences through Bessel-channel interference in a driven two-level model.
AI.conclusion: The framework recovers known results (Bessel-weighted plasmon-loss, diffusive combs, PINEM Bessel ladder) in specific limits while providing a unified theoretical description. A no-double-counting prescription is provided for combining coherent and incoherent channels. The theory applies to structured targets, inhomogeneous fields, and exhibits off-diagonal Floquet coherences through Bessel-channel interference.

title: Recrystallization as a tool to characterize and control the properties of cold sprayed materials: case study on 316L steel
comment: Manuscript for a submission to JTST
summary: Owing to the unique buildup mechanisms, recrystallization in cold sprayed materials significantly differs from that in conventional counterparts. In this study, the relationship between deformation-induced microstructural heterogeneity, recrystallization behavior, and mechanical properties of cold sprayed materials was investigated using EBSD and nanoindentation. The 316L stainless steel was selected as a model material. The deposit was characterized in its as-sprayed condition and after annealing at temperatures between 900 and 1100 K. Thermomechanical estimates suggest that locally, temperature can rise over 1000 K and very high dislocation densities (up to 1017 m-2) form at particle boundaries during impact, providing a strong driving force for subsequent recrystallization. The EBSD observations confirmed the intense defect accumulation and grain fragmentation localized near the particle interfaces. Recrystallization initiated preferentially in these highly strained areas after annealing at 1000 K and progressed with increasing temperature and holding time, leading to complete recrystallization after 1 h at 1100 K. The recrystallized grain-size distribution was well described by a heavy-tailed log-normal distribution, which indicates extremely heterogeneous strain partitioning generated during particle impacts. Nanoindentation measurements showed that the high hardness of the cold sprayed deposit remained largely unchanged after annealing at 900 K but gradually decreased as recrystallization progressed. We further demonstrate that controlled post-spray recrystallization can serve as a powerful tool for characterizing deformation during deposition and for tailoring the microstructure and mechanical properties of cold-sprayed materials.

AI.tldr: This study investigates recrystallization in cold sprayed 316L stainless steel, revealing unique deformation mechanisms due to high-strain-rate impact. The research connects deformation-induced microstructural heterogeneity with recrystallization behavior and mechanical properties using EBSD and nanoindentation techniques.
AI.motivation: Cold spray materials exhibit unique buildup mechanisms that differ significantly from conventional manufacturing methods. Understanding the recrystallization behavior in cold sprayed materials is crucial for controlling microstructure and mechanical properties, but the underlying deformation mechanisms and their effects during annealing remain poorly understood.
AI.method: EBSD (Electron Backscatter Diffraction) and nanoindentation were used to investigate the relationship between deformation-induced microstructural heterogeneity, recrystallization behavior, and mechanical properties. The 316L stainless steel was studied in as-sprayed condition and after annealing at temperatures between 900-1100 K. Thermomechanical estimates were also performed to understand the temperature and dislocation density during impact.
AI.result: Local temperatures can rise over 1000 K during impact with dislocation densities up to 10^17 m^-2 forming at particle boundaries. EBSD confirmed intense defect accumulation and grain fragmentation near particle interfaces. Recrystallization initiated preferentially in highly strained areas at 1000 K and progressed with increasing temperature/time, achieving complete recrystallization after 1 h at 1100 K. The recrystallized grain-size distribution followed a heavy-tailed log-normal distribution, indicating extremely heterogeneous strain partitioning. Hardness remained unchanged at 900 K but decreased as recrystallization progressed.
AI.conclusion: Controlled post-spray recrystallization is a powerful tool for both characterizing deformation during deposition and tailoring the microstructure and mechanical properties of cold-sprayed materials. This provides a pathway for engineering materials with optimized performance through understanding and controlling the recrystallization process.

title: Magnetic-Order-Driven Nonlinear Photocurrents in PT-Broken Antiferromagnetic MnS2 and Altermagnetic MnSe2
summary: Nonlinear photocurrent responses generally require inversion-symmetry breaking, but its origin can be magnetic rather than structural. In this study, we investigate the bulk photovoltaic effect in antiferromagnetic MnS2 and altermagnetic MnSe2, two pyrite-type semiconductors whose magnetic ordering breaks inversion symmetry P and its combination with time reversal PT, while the accompanying lattice distortion is minute. We calculate the shift current (SC) and injection current (IC) responses under linearly and circularly polarized light with and without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and identify their symmetry-allowed tensor components using the corresponding magnetic and spin point groups, respectively. Linear SC and circular IC are symmetry-allowed in both MnS2 and MnSe2 irrespective of SOC, whereas linear IC and circular SC remain forbidden in MnS2 but become allowed in MnSe2 only when SOC is included. These results highlight the importance of SOC and the corresponding MPG analysis for a complete description of nonlinear charge photocurrents in magnetic materials. Beyond charge responses, MnSe2 supports linear shift and circular injection spin photocurrents in the nonrelativistic limit, whereas all spin-photocurrent responses are forbidden in MnS2. Our findings therefore establish inversion symmetry breaking induced by compensated magnetic order as a route to generating and controlling nonlinear photocurrents.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the bulk photovoltaic effect in antiferromagnetic MnS2 and altermagnetic MnSe2 (pyrite-type semiconductors) where magnetic ordering breaks inversion symmetry. Using symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations, the authors examine shift current (SC) and injection current (IC) responses under polarized light, finding that linear SC and circular IC are allowed in both materials regardless of spin-orbit coupling (SOC), while linear IC and circular SC become allowed in MnSe2 only with SOC. Spin photocurrents are also predicted for MnSe2.
AI.motivation: Nonlinear photocurrent responses typically require inversion-symmetry breaking, which can originate from structural or magnetic sources. This study aims to explore whether magnetic ordering alone (without significant lattice distortion) can enable bulk photovoltaic effects in compensated antiferromagnets, and to understand the role of spin-orbit coupling in enabling such responses.
AI.method: The authors calculate shift current (SC) and injection current (IC) responses under linearly and circularly polarized light using first-principles methods, with and without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). They identify symmetry-allowed tensor components using corresponding magnetic point groups (MPGs) and spin point groups.
AI.result: Linear SC and circular IC are symmetry-allowed in both MnS2 and MnSe2 regardless of SOC. Linear IC and circular SC are forbidden in MnS2 but become allowed in MnSe2 only when SOC is included. For spin photocurrents, MnSe2 supports linear shift and circular injection spin photocurrents in the nonrelativistic limit, while all spin-photocurrent responses are forbidden in MnS2.
AI.conclusion: Inversion symmetry breaking induced by compensated magnetic order (as in antiferromagnets and altermagnets) provides a viable route to generating and controlling nonlinear photocurrents. SOC and corresponding MPG analysis are essential for a complete description of nonlinear charge photocurrents in magnetic materials.

title: Symmetry Engineering Enables Deterministic Ensemble Polarization Control in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
summary: Optical polarization is a key degree of freedom in quantum photonic and sensing technologies, enabling efficient light--matter coupling and directional emission. However, in defect ensemble-based quantum systems, orientational averaging across many defects suppresses optical anisotropy and eliminates a deterministic polarization axis. Here, symmetry engineering is introduced as a strategy to restore collective optical anisotropy in negatively charged boron vacancy (V_B^-) ensembles hosted in hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN). By imposing anisotropic in-plane tensile strain through lithographically defined nano-ridge arrays, in-plane symmetry is broken and the ensemble emission dipole is aligned with the ridge-defined strain symmetry axis. Polarization-resolved photoluminescence reveals that the polarization visibility scales with the magnitude of strain anisotropy, while the emission orientation rigidly follows the engineered symmetry axis across devices with varying strain direction. This deterministic alignment is independent of crystal orientation, establishing the optical foundation for polarization-defined ensemble spin readout and programmable photonic integration in two-dimensional quantum materials

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to restore optical anisotropy in boron vacancy (V_B^-) defect ensembles in hexagonal boron nitride by engineering symmetry through anisotropic in-plane tensile strain using nano-ridge arrays, enabling deterministic polarization control for quantum applications.
AI.motivation: In defect ensemble-based quantum systems, orientational averaging across many defects suppresses optical anisotropy and eliminates a deterministic polarization axis, limiting their applicability in quantum photonic and sensing technologies that require efficient light-matter coupling and directional emission.
AI.method: The researchers imposed anisotropic in-plane tensile strain through lithographically defined nano-ridge arrays to break in-plane symmetry, aligning the ensemble emission dipole with the ridge-defined strain symmetry axis. They used polarization-resolved photoluminescence to characterize the results.
AI.result: Polarization visibility scales with the magnitude of strain anisotropy, while emission orientation rigidly follows the engineered symmetry axis across devices with varying strain direction. This alignment is independent of crystal orientation.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes the optical foundation for polarization-defined ensemble spin readout and programmable photonic integration in two-dimensional quantum materials, providing a strategy for controlling optical polarization in defect ensemble systems.
